_comment: The rule inventory (feature 015, FR-001). One entry per distinct failure-emission site in
a grading script. 'emitAnchor' is a literal substring of the message as it appears in the
script source — it is how Coverage.Tests.ps1 ties an inventory entry to the line that
emits it, so a rule that is deleted or reworded is caught rather than silently orphaned.
Phase 1 inventories Invoke-StructureCheck only; phase 2 adds the two GAP rules it closes; phases 3 and 4 complete it.
DIRECTIONS. Every rule has a 'fail' case and a 'pass' case, and from T029 on those names
mean 'the condition the rule names HOLDS' and 'the nearest state in which it does not'.
For the adverse rules — the great majority — that is the same thing as failing and
passing. It is not for the inert and affirmative verdicts scope-check-repos.ps1 emits: a
'fail' case for 'n/a (declared but not present here)' exits 0, because the rule under test
IS the n/a. Naming those directions after the exit code would have meant leaving the inert
verdicts out of the inventory, and the inert verdicts are precisely what SC-004 and GAP-027
are about — a state in which nothing was graded must not read as a graded pass.
EXEMPTIONS (FR-004, added in phase 6). A rule MAY carry an 'exemption' field instead of a
pass/fail pair. The field is the written reason, it is printed on every run, and the rule
stays in the inventory so the site cannot be reworded or deleted unnoticed. An exemption is
not 'not yet covered': it is a stated position that a faithful fixture cannot be built, and
every one of them says what would be needed instead.

rules.summary: a digest on disk does not match what its sources produce
rules.law: CLAUDE.md Task-Scoped Reading (a digest is never a source-of-truth rung, so it may never drift from the law it digests)
rules.notes: The pass direction over this recipe is the GAP-025 demonstration: a '<!--' inside an inline code span opened a phantom comment that swallowed every later marker, so a CORRECT digest was reported stale and a regenerated one silently lost rules.

rules.summary: the manifest names a document that is not on disk
rules.notes: Skipping it would shrink the pack’s digest to whatever survived and still report it fresh — the shape of every defect this script guards against.

rules.summary: a digest marker carries no text
rules.notes: An empty bullet says a rule exists here and declines to say what it is.

rules.summary: a marker exceeds MaxDigestLineLength (120 chars)
rules.notes: The bound is what keeps a digest a digest: an orientation aid stops being one when its lines are as long as the law they point at.

rules.summary: a line begins like a marker and breaks the exact grammar
rules.notes: Fail-closed. Vanishing silently would leave the check enforcing the ABSENCE of a rule whose author believed it was marked — the same choice scope-check.ps1 makes for a Territory marker with no colon.

rules.summary: a pack name is not a safe filename fragment
rules.notes: The name is interpolated into a write path, so fail-closed validation is what stops a manifest routing a write outside docs/digests/.

rules.summary: two packs declare the same name
rules.notes: Both write the same file, so the second pack’s law is swallowed whole by the first with nothing in the output to say so.

rules.summary: a pack exceeds MaxDigestContentLines (40 bullets)
rules.notes: Past the bound a digest is a second copy of the law. Its digest is deliberately NOT treated as an orphan (review F1): the fix is trimming markers, not deleting the file.

rules.summary: a pack carries markers and its digest was never generated
rules.law: feature 010 contract specs/010-law-digests/contracts/digest-checks.md; CLAUDE.md Task-Scoped Reading (a digest is never a source-of-truth rung)
rules.notes: The digest is linked from CLAUDE.md, so a reader following the pointer would find nothing and conclude the pack has no law.

rules.summary: a *-digest.md exists that no manifest pack produces
rules.law: feature 010 contract specs/010-law-digests/contracts/digest-checks.md; CLAUDE.md Task-Scoped Reading (a digest is never a source-of-truth rung)
rules.notes: Law-shaped text nothing regenerates drifts from the moment it is written. Contrast DIGEST-018: generate mode reports the same file as a NOTE, because an author mid-edit is not a tree under CI.

rules.summary: no digest manifest exists and no digests do either
rules.notes: The machinery ships INERT and arms itself the moment a project marks its own law. An OK here would be a check reporting success over a feature nobody turned on — SC-004 exactly.

rules.summary: the manifest is gone but digest files remain
rules.notes: Not an inert project — a project whose manifest was deleted, leaving digests that can never again be regenerated or verified. One file on disk separates this from DIGEST-011 and the verdicts are opposite.

rules.summary: the manifest is absent when generation is asked for
rules.notes: The author asked for digests and nothing says which to build, so the script refuses rather than writing a guess.

rules.summary: a manifest exists and no document carries a marker
rules.notes: The second inert state, kept distinct from DIGEST-011 so the reason in the output is the true one.

rules.summary: every digest matches what its sources produce
rules.law: feature 010 contract specs/010-law-digests/contracts/digest-checks.md; CLAUDE.md Task-Scoped Reading (a digest is never a source-of-truth rung)
rules.notes: The affirmative verdict, and its counts are its substance: OK over nought digests and nought markers would be the inert state wearing a success message.

rules.summary: generation finds no markers and writes nothing
rules.emitAnchor: no digest markers found — nothing to generate
rules.notes: Writing an empty digest instead would create a file -Check then has to defend.

rules.summary: a digest file is written
rules.notes: One line per file, because an author needs to know WHICH files changed under them — a single summary leaves a surprising diff unexplained.

rules.summary: an orphan digest is present while generating
rules.notes: A NOTE, and the run still succeeds — the same file DIGEST-010 fails in check mode. Generate mode never deletes a file it did not write, so it warns about what will fail later instead.

rules.summary: generation completes over a healthy tree
rules.notes: Paired with a run stopped by a source issue, whose own line states NOTHING WRITTEN: a generator that half-wrote and then failed would leave some digests fresh and some not, with no record of which.

rules.summary: a phase commit touches a file outside the phase's declared Territory
rules.law: CLAUDE.md Workflow step 7; constitution VI (gate 4, the machine scope check)
rules.notes: Two emission sites, declared: the Micro arm reads Territory from the mini-spec and the Standard arm reads it from tasks.md, and both print the same sentence. Declared rather than narrowed because it IS one rule - what differs is which document the territory came from, not what is refused. Both directions of this recipe carry a DECORATED Territory marker - the GAP-026 demonstration. Get-Territory anchored on '**Territory**:' and read an annotated marker as no declaration, so the check WARNed and exited 0 having graded nothing.

rules.summary: a phase declares no Territory while another phase in the same tasks.md declares one
rules.law: constitution VI (gate 4); FR-015 - the pre-006 compatibility WARN covers a document that predates the convention, not a phase that skipped it
rules.emitAnchor: but another phase in that file declares one
rules.notes: Before FR-015 this was a non-blocking WARN and the check exited 0 having graded nothing - GAP-027's species, reached through GAP-026's door.

rules.summary: a **Territory** line whose annotation wraps carries no colon and declares nothing
rules.law: constitution VI (gate 4); FR-014's intent - a decorated marker must not silently declare nothing
rules.emitDescription: the near-miss FAIL added by T019a
rules.emitAnchor: but has no ':' on that line
rules.notes: Phase 2 review F3. specs/014-amendment-authority/tasks.md:322 is still this shape. Fixed by making the near-miss loud rather than by joining continuation lines - the pattern build-digests.ps1 uses for a malformed digest marker.

rules.summary: a commit on a feature branch deletes its own declaration file
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4; 006 review F2
rules.emitAnchor: a feature's declaration files must never be deleted on its branch
rules.notes: Runs BEFORE phase attribution on purpose, so a commit carrying no 'phase N' token cannot smuggle the deletion past the grader. Pairs with SCOPE-005, the same move wearing a rename.

rules.summary: a commit renames its own declaration file away
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4; 006 review F2, phase 2 review F3
rules.emitAnchor: away — a feature's declaration files must never be deleted or renamed
rules.notes: 'A rename away is a delete wearing a costume.' Needed the harness to learn 'git mv' (the recipe's new 'rename'): an add-plus-delete fixture would have exercised SCOPE-004's arm and left this one untested while looking like coverage.

rules.summary: a Micro mini-spec carries more than one Territory block
rules.emitAnchor: (a Micro feature declares exactly one feature-global block)
rules.notes: Two declarations are not a wider declaration, they are an ambiguous one - and the lane's five-file cap cannot be applied to a pair.

rules.summary: a Micro territory entry is not repo-relative
rules.emitAnchor: invalid territory entry '$bad' (entries must be repo-relative, no '..'); $microPromote
rules.notes: The sibling of enforcement-pack's MICRO-009, and the reason that one mattered: both graders read the same block through the same parser, so this pins that scope-check refuses the entry rather than either grader dropping it.

rules.summary: a Micro feature declares no usable Territory block at all
rules.notes: The one place the two lanes deliberately disagree: an absent declaration is a non-blocking WARN on Standard (pre-006 compatibility) and a hard FAIL on Micro, because no pre-Micro feature exists to grandfather.

rules.summary: the territory declaration is missing at the parent while the feature directory exists
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4; research D3, 006 review F2 (anti-retroactivity)
rules.emitAnchor: is missing at the parent while specs/
rules.notes: T028's named rule, and the load-bearing one: the declaration is read from the commit's PARENT so an amendment only governs commits made after it lands. Falling back to the commit's own blob is legal ONLY for a true claim commit, where the parent lacks the whole feature directory. The fail case restores tasks.md IN the phase commit - a declaration post-dating the commit it would legalise; the pass case restores it in its own commit first, which is the remediation the message names.

rules.summary: a phase declares more than one Territory marker in tasks.md
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4; 006 review F8
rules.emitAnchor: more than one **Territory** marker for phase
rules.notes: The Standard-lane sibling of SCOPE-006, and the reason exactly-one-per-phase is graded rather than assumed.

rules.summary: a Standard territory entry is not repo-relative
rules.notes: Territory is graded by -like matching against repo-relative commit paths, so a non-repo-relative entry can never match anything: a declaration that silently declares nothing. THE ANCHOR CARRIES ITS CLOSING QUOTE, and that is not fussiness - the Micro arm (SCOPE-007) prints the identical sentence and then continues into the promotion remediation, so the natural anchor matched both sites. Caught by the anchor-ambiguity assertion written in phase 3's T023 for exactly this, on its first real encounter: without it SCOPE-011 would have silently marked the Micro site covered by a Standard fixture that never reaches it.

rules.summary: a Territory marker is declared with an empty entry list
rules.emitAnchor: but the entry list is empty (declare the paths, or remove the marker)
rules.notes: NOT the pre-006 compatibility case: an ABSENT declaration WARNs and passes, a declared-and-empty one FAILs, because the author said 'here is my territory' and then named nothing. The pair with SCOPE-002 is what makes that distinction testable rather than merely documented.

rules.summary: the commit named for grading does not resolve to a commit
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); constitution IV
rules.emitAnchor: ERROR '$Sha' does not resolve to a commit
rules.notes: 'rev-parse --short' echoes an unknown sha back rather than failing, so the exit code is the only thing separating a real commit from a typo.

rules.summary: the commit is a merge commit, which authored nothing
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); constitution IV; feature 012 D7
rules.notes: Grading a merge would charge one phase for every file both sides touched.

rules.summary: the commit carries no 'phase N' token, so no declaration governs it
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); constitution IV
rules.notes: Territory is declared per phase. The declaration-deletion guard runs ABOVE this, so a token-less commit cannot smuggle a deletion past it.

rules.summary: a Micro commit is wholly inside the territory its mini-spec declares
rules.law: constitution X (Micro lane); Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); constitution IV
rules.notes: The affirmative verdict for the Micro lane. The provenance suffix is the only thing in the output that says the declaration came from spec.md rather than a tasks.md the feature does not have.

rules.summary: tasks.md exists neither at the commit nor at its parent
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); constitution IV; feature 006 pre-006 compatibility
rules.emitAnchor: not found at the commit or its parent
rules.notes: A history predating the convention entirely. Non-blocking, and the WARN is the whole verdict: nothing was graded, and the line names the file that would have to exist.

rules.summary: tasks.md declares no Territory anywhere, at any phase
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); constitution IV; feature 006 FR-015
rules.emitAnchor: no territory declared for phase $phaseN in $tasksRel (declare territory
rules.notes: The one state in which an undeclared path still exits 0. SCOPE-002 sits beside it: the moment any other phase declares, the mercy stops applying.

rules.summary: every path in the commit is inside the declared territory
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); constitution IV
rules.notes: The affirmative verdict the check exists to be able to give. The file count is part of it — a PASS over nought files is a pass nobody should trust, which is phase 5’s ungraded state.

rules.summary: the current branch cannot be read from the repository
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); constitution IV; docs/sdlc/branch-strategy.md
rules.emitAnchor: ERROR cannot determine the current branch
rules.notes: Reachable with an unborn HEAD. Exits 1 rather than guessing: the lane selects every rule below it.

rules.summary: HEAD is detached, so the branch name is the literal word HEAD
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); constitution IV; docs/sdlc/branch-strategy.md
rules.notes: The CI shape. Non-blocking, and it names the flag that fixes it, because a wrapper omitting -Branch classifies every run wrongly. WORD CHANGED in the phase-5 remediation (review F1): this site reported a run that graded nothing, and did it in a word that meant something else. The case is unchanged except for the verdict word it expects - the before-state is the previous revision of this rule's expected.txt, which is the D11 record for this conversion.

rules.summary: the branch is a fix/, chore/ or docs/ lane, which has no phases
rules.law: constitution X (the Lite lane); Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); constitution IV
rules.emitAnchor: lane — enforcement-pack's Lite-lane checks apply instead
rules.notes: Inapplicable rather than skipped, and the line names the check that grades the lane instead.

rules.summary: the branch is the trunk, where no feature declares Territory
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); constitution IV; docs/sdlc/branch-strategy.md
rules.notes: CI runs on main too. This line is what keeps a main build from reporting a scope pass it never made.

rules.summary: the branch is not NNN-shaped, so it maps to no spec directory
rules.law: CLAUDE.md Feature Structure; Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); constitution IV
rules.emitAnchor: is not a numbered feature branch
rules.notes: The branch name is quoted back, because the name itself is the thing to fix.

rules.summary: under -All, no merge base with main can be resolved
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); constitution IV; GAP-027
rules.emitAnchor: UNGRADED could not resolve a merge base with main
rules.notes: A clone whose trunk is called something else. NOTHING is checked and the line says so — the exact shape GAP-027 is about; phase 5 reconsiders its exit code. WORD CHANGED in the phase-5 remediation (review F1): this site reported a run that graded nothing, and did it in a word that meant something else. The case is unchanged except for the verdict word it expects - the before-state is the previous revision of this rule's expected.txt, which is the D11 record for this conversion.

rules.summary: under -All, the range since the merge base is empty
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); constitution IV; GAP-027
rules.notes: The one line in this script that says 'pass' about a run that examined no commit. WORD CHANGED in the phase-5 remediation (review F1): this site reported a run that graded nothing, and did it in a word that meant something else. The case is unchanged except for the verdict word it expects - the before-state is the previous revision of this rule's expected.txt, which is the D11 record for this conversion.

rules.summary: a Lite-lane branch touches a prohibited category
rules.law: constitution X (the Lite lane is for changes that need no specification)
rules.emitAnchor: a prohibited category for the Lite lane
rules.notes: Fires once per file per matching category, so one file can fire it twice.

rules.summary: a Lite-lane branch changes more files than the abuse guard allows
rules.law: constitution X (the Lite lane is bounded by size as well as by category)
rules.notes: The pass case sits exactly AT the guard (25 files), which pins the comparison as '>' rather than '>=' - a fixture, not a comment, now holds that boundary.

rules.summary: a Lite-lane branch touches a migration path, regardless of file count
rules.emitAnchor: migrations are always prohibited on the Lite lane
rules.notes: Deliberately overlaps the category rule: one migration file fires both, because a config that dropped the schema globs would silence the category rule alone.

rules.summary: a plan.md or tasks.md exists while spec.md still declares Micro
rules.law: constitution X, Micro lane (promotion is all-or-nothing)
rules.emitAnchor: exists while spec.md still declares Micro
rules.notes: Fires once per document present, so a half-promoted feature reports both.

rules.summary: a mini-spec declares a gate batch
rules.law: constitution X, Micro lane (exactly one phase, so nothing to batch)
rules.emitAnchor: a Micro feature is exactly one phase; there is nothing to batch

rules.summary: a mini-spec carries more than one feature-global Territory block
rules.emitAnchor: **Territory** markers — a Micro feature declares exactly one
rules.notes: scope-check.ps1 FAILs duplicates too; the two are deliberately aligned (014 phase 2 review F7).

rules.summary: a Micro Territory declares more files than the cap allows
rules.emitAnchor: territory entries — a Micro feature's Territory covers at most
rules.notes: The pass case sits exactly AT five entries, pinning the comparison as '>' rather than '>='.

rules.summary: a Micro Territory entry is a glob or a subtree rather than a literal path
rules.emitAnchor: is a glob or subtree — Micro territory entries must be literal
rules.notes: Without this the file cap is unenforceable: one glob covers any number of files.

rules.summary: a Micro phase changes more lines than the lane's hard bound
rules.emitAnchor: a Micro phase changes at most
rules.notes: The total across every commit carrying the phase token, so splitting the change over remediation commits cannot defeat it. The fail case also trips PhaseSizeWarning, which is how the WARN and the FAIL are shown to be different rules reading the same number.

rules.summary: a Micro branch carries commits for more than one phase
rules.notes: Distinct phase NUMBERS are counted, not commits: the pass case has two commits both carrying phase 1, which is remediation and stays legal.

rules.summary: a phase commit exceeds the phase-size guideline
rules.notes: The kit's only WARN rule: it does not change the exit code, and the pair proves that - both directions expect exit 0 and differ only in whether the warning line is printed. Phase 5 settles where WARN sits in the vocabulary (D4).

rules.summary: a mini-spec's **Territory** line carries no colon because its annotation wraps
rules.law: constitution X, Micro lane; FR-014's intent — a decorated marker must not silently declare nothing
rules.emitAnchor: begins '**Territory**' but has no ':' on that line
rules.notes: The Micro half of T019a. Both graders now say the same thing about the same malformed line, because both now call the same parser.

rules.summary: a Micro territory entry that escapes the repository is refused, not dropped
rules.law: constitution X, Micro lane (the five-file cap); FR-014
rules.emitAnchor: is not repo-relative — Micro territory entries must be repo-relative paths
rules.notes: Found in the phase 3 diff review, and introduced BY phase 3: T020a replaced the inline parser with Get-Territory, whose Invalid field the caller did not read, so an absolute or '..' entry stopped counting toward the cap and was reported by nobody - while scope-check.ps1 FAILed the same entry in the same block. Demonstrated failing first (D11): before the fix the fail recipe exited 0 printing 'enforcement-pack: OK'. A regression a task's own success criteria would not have caught, because T020a's criterion was 'the copy is gone'.

rules.summary: a Critical feature in solo mode carries no second-model review
rules.emitAnchor: second-model-review.md is missing (required for Critical features
rules.notes: Solo mode is the default: no kit-adoption.json means no roster, and the substitute reviewer is the only evidence this lane accepts.

rules.summary: the second-model review exists only in the working tree, so no clock has started
rules.emitAnchor: has no git history — cannot verify the cooling-off period
rules.notes: The first rule the recipe's new 'uncommitted' support made provable; until then this state could not be built at all.

rules.summary: the second-model review is younger than the cooling-off period
rules.notes: The pair sits either side of 24h by half an hour (23.5 / 24.5), using the recipe's new 'hoursAgo' back-dating. Relative, not absolute: an absolute date would make this fixture expire.

rules.summary: a Critical feature in team mode carries no human PR review
rules.emitAnchor: requires the independent human review itself, not the solo substitute
rules.notes: Team mode is selected by two or more names in kit-adoption.json. The solo substitute does not satisfy it.

rules.summary: the human PR review exists only in the working tree
rules.emitAnchor: is not committed — evidence that exists only in a working tree is not evidence
rules.notes: The check reads the committed blob, not the file: copying the template in early and filling it locally at review time used to pass on content the branch does not carry (013 phase 4 re-review, N1).

rules.summary: the human PR review has no visible Review Provenance section
rules.emitAnchor: has no visible '## Review Provenance' section
rules.notes: Visible means rendered: a section inside an HTML comment does not count, and an unterminated comment earlier in the file hides everything after it.

rules.summary: the Review Provenance section leaves Reviewer or Owner unfilled
rules.notes: Fires once per missing identity. Half a pair proves nothing, because the rule the evidence exists for is that the two are different people.

rules.summary: Reviewer or Owner is still the template's bracketed placeholder
rules.notes: A bare [bracketed] value only. '[Name](mailto:...)' is an ordinary markdown link and must not be read as a placeholder.

rules.summary: the human reviewer of a Critical feature is also its owner
rules.notes: The rule the entire team arm exists for. Compared case-insensitively.

rules.summary: the Review Provenance section is missing the verbatim attestation sentence
rules.emitAnchor: human-pr-review.md is missing the verbatim attestation sentence
rules.notes: Matched inside the provenance slice, not the whole file: an attestation quoted in an unrelated comment used to satisfy it.

rules.summary: the Gate Batching value is neither 'none' nor a span
the declared batch span runs backwards
rules.emitAnchor: the span is reversed (N must not exceed M)

rules.summary: the declared batch covers more phases than the cap allows
rules.notes: The pass case sits exactly AT three phases, pinning the comparison as '>' rather than '>='.

rules.summary: a Critical feature declares a gate batch
rules.emitAnchor: declares a gate batch on a Critical feature
rules.notes: Both directions carry a valid, cooled-off second-model review so the case reports this rule and nothing else.

rules.summary: the Gate Certification value is not one of the two legal values
rules.notes: On a Micro feature the declaration's home is the mini-spec rather than plan.md; that arm is covered in phase 4.

rules.summary: a Critical feature declares ci-held certification
rules.emitAnchor: on a Critical feature — Critical features MUST NOT use CI-held certification

rules.summary: a commit amends an approved feature document with no conforming approver record
rules.law: constitution I, Amendment authority (you never approve your own amendment)
rules.emitAnchor: after approval with no conforming approver record
rules.notes: Twelve directions, because the rule is mostly made of what it does NOT fire on. Four fail: 'fail' (no record), 'fail-hidden-record' (a correct record inside an unterminated HTML comment - H1), 'fail-placeholder' (an unfilled slot, which prints what it rejected - D6), 'fail-rename-content' (a contract renamed and reinterpreted in one commit - H3). Six pass: 'pass' (a conforming record) and the exemptions - creation (D2), a ticked checkbox (D3c), Draft to Approved (D3d), a renumbered feature directory (J3), and 'pass-rename-identical', the sibling of 'fail-rename-content' that pins a byte-identical move as no amendment at all. Two more cover git reality (T026): 'fail-nonascii' (core.quotepath) and 'pass-merge' (a second parent, D7). Every fixture commits a stub scripts/enforcement-pack.ps1 defining this function, because the D2b boundary asks the parent tree whether the check existed - without it every commit reports as pre-boundary and the fixture grades nothing while printing green.

rules.summary: a conforming record names an approver the commit message does not
rules.law: constitution I, Amendment authority; plan D5 (half the record lives where a later edit cannot reach)
rules.emitAnchor: as the approver of its change to
rules.notes: The pass and fail cases carry the SAME record in the SAME file and differ only in the commit message, which is the point of D5: the document half can be written at any time, the message half only at commit time.

rules.summary: the boundary cannot be computed because the clone is shallow
rules.law: constitution I, Amendment authority; FR-011 (silence is not compliance)
rules.emitAnchor: this is a shallow clone, so the boundary
rules.notes: Asked of git directly ('rev-parse --is-shallow-repository') rather than inferred from the base, because a shallow clone can still resolve origin/main - a base that looks fine says nothing about whether the history behind it is present. Phase 4 review F1: this used to return bare, printing nothing and exiting 0, which is indistinguishable from a branch that is legitimately pre-boundary.

rules.summary: there is no integration branch to compute a range against
rules.emitAnchor: no integration branch to diff against. Either neither
rules.notes: One site, two causes - no ref resolves, or one resolves and shares no commit with HEAD - and the message says it does not distinguish them rather than naming a cause it did not test. The fixture builds the first; the second needs unrelated histories and is the same emission.

rules.summary: a commit's parent cannot be read, so whether it predates the check is unknown
rules.law: constitution I, Amendment authority; T080 (absence must be proven, not inferred)
rules.emitAnchor: is not readable in this clone, so whether it predates the check is unknown
rules.notes: Built with 'truncateBlob': an object that is in the store and cannot be inflated. This is the damage mode review G1 measured - 'cat-file -e' and 'cat-file -s' both report it fine, and only reading the body fails where a reader fails. Unknown reported as 'predates the check' is a wrong reason printed green.

rules.summary: a run with no computable base says that nothing was compared
rules.law: FR-009 (the Lite lane must not newly fail on a null base) and FR-011; GAP-027
rules.emitAnchor: was compared — each check that reads the diff either graded an empty file list
rules.notes: GAP-027's own line. Both directions exit 0 - what differs is whether the run admits it compared nothing - so the fail direction is the shape the roadmap describes: a fix/ branch on a baseless clone, green, having graded nothing. Phase 5 (T039-T041) gives this an UNGRADED verdict state; when it rewords this line the stale-anchor assertion will say so, which is the point of inventorying it now rather than after.

rules.summary: a branch whose name matches no lane is failed on the name, not passed on the silence
rules.emitAnchor: does not match a known taxonomy (NNN-*, fix/*, chore/*, docs/*)
rules.notes: The last arm of the dispatch chain, and the one that decides what an unrecognised name means. 'feature/thing' reaches no lane at all, so every scripted check is skipped: without this rule the run would be indistinguishable from a clean one. Pass and fail differ only in the branch name (plan D10) - 'chore/thing' over the identical tree.

rules.summary: a review file is in the branch diff but absent from the working tree
rules.law: DoD gate 5; constitution VI - provenance that cannot be read has not been verified
rules.emitAnchor: is in the branch diff but missing from the working tree
rules.notes: The fail-closed arm. Built with the recipe's 'uncommittedDelete', added here: the commit-to-commit diff still names the file while the working tree does not have it, and no recipe could produce that state before. An open-coded 'continue' with no failure would have read as green on exactly the branch that deleted its own evidence.

rules.summary: an AI review added on the branch has no Reviewer Provenance section
rules.law: DoD gate 5 (the review must be produced by a fresh-context agent or second model, and say so)
rules.notes: Only files ADDED or RENAMED-TO in the branch diff are graded, so reviews predating the verification pack stay grandfathered - the pass direction of every rule here also holds that filter in place.

rules.summary: the Reviewer Provenance section carries no filled **Reviewer** line
rules.emitAnchor: has no filled '**Reviewer**:' line inside its Reviewer Provenance section
rules.notes: Both directions carry a FILLED '**Reviewer**:' line in the document header, which is the phase 2 review's F1: the header must never shadow the block. The fail case is green to a reader skimming the top of the document and red to the check, which is the whole point of slicing the section out first.

rules.summary: the reviewer is the implementer, or is still a template placeholder
rules.law: DoD gate 5 (the implementing agent must not review its own diff); constitution VI
rules.emitAnchor: the implementing agent must not review its own diff
rules.notes: One emission site, two conditions, so it carries a third direction: 'fail' is the unfilled bracketed placeholder and 'fail-implementer' is the self-review the law is actually about. A pass/fail pair alone would have covered the site while leaving the condition that matters untested.

rules.summary: the verbatim attestation sentence is absent
rules.emitAnchor: ReviewProvenance: $file is missing the verbatim attestation sentence
rules.notes: The fail case PARAPHRASES the sentence rather than deleting it - 'did not write the code under review'. A deletion would pass this fixture for the wrong reason: it is the near-miss that tests whether the match is verbatim.

rules.summary: a required feature document is missing from the spec directory
rules.law: CLAUDE.md Feature Structure; constitution I (Specification First)
rules.emitAnchor: is missing (every NNN-* branch requires spec.md, plan.md, and tasks.md
rules.notes: Fires once per missing document. A Micro feature requires spec.md alone.

rules.summary: spec.md carries no Delivery Level header
rules.law: constitution X (Controlled Delivery — the level selects the lane)
rules.notes: Read from visible text only: a header inside an HTML comment sets no lane.

rules.summary: the Delivery Level header is unfilled or off-menu
rules.law: constitution X (legal values: Lite, Micro, Standard, Critical)
rules.emitAnchor: **Delivery Level** header is unfilled or invalid
rules.notes: This is the only validation the level gets today — spelling, not judgement. GAP-023 is the missing half.

rules.summary: no code repositories are declared, so there is nothing to grade
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); docs/sdlc/repository-strategy.md; feature 012 D2
rules.notes: The kit itself and every single-repo adoption land here. An inert verdict, counted as a rule on purpose: printing a bare OK for a run that reached no code is SC-004's exact failure.

rules.summary: kit-adoption.json is not valid JSON
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); docs/sdlc/repository-strategy.md; adoption/updating.md (the record’s shape)
rules.emitAnchor: WARN kit-adoption.json is not valid JSON
rules.notes: The record is the only statement of which repositories exist. Unreadable means unknown, and unknown is reported twice — here, and again as the run-level n/a.

rules.summary: codeRepos is present but is not an array
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); docs/sdlc/repository-strategy.md; adoption/updating.md
rules.emitAnchor: WARN kit-adoption.json codeRepos is not an array
rules.notes: A bare string is what an author writes when there is one repository. Enumerating it would look for repositories named after its characters.

rules.summary: a codeRepos entry is a path, a traversal or a drive prefix rather than a plain directory name
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); docs/sdlc/repository-strategy.md; feature 012 phase 1 review F7
rules.notes: The doctor FAILs these; the grader refuses them independently, because a code repository’s own CI may never run the doctor. One bad entry does not stop the run.

rules.summary: -Repo names a repository the record does not declare
rules.notes: Narrowing a run to nothing is an ERROR with exit 1, never a quiet success — the caller asked for a verdict and would otherwise get silence.

rules.summary: the current branch cannot be read from the repository
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); docs/sdlc/repository-strategy.md; docs/sdlc/branch-strategy.md (the lane decides the rules)
rules.emitAnchor: ERROR cannot determine the current branch
rules.notes: Reachable with an unborn HEAD. The lane selects every rule below it, so a check that cannot name the branch stops instead of guessing.

rules.summary: HEAD is detached, so the branch name is the literal word HEAD
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); docs/sdlc/repository-strategy.md; docs/sdlc/branch-strategy.md
rules.notes: The CI shape: a job that checked out a sha. Non-blocking, but it names the flag that fixes it, because a wrapper that omits -Branch here classifies every run wrongly. WORD CHANGED in the phase-5 remediation (review F1): this site reported a run that graded nothing, and did it in a word that meant something else. The case is unchanged except for the verdict word it expects - the before-state is the previous revision of this rule's expected.txt, which is the D11 record for this conversion.

rules.summary: the branch is a fix/, chore/ or docs/ lane, which has no phases
rules.law: constitution X (Controlled Delivery — the Lite lane); Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); docs/sdlc/repository-strategy.md
rules.emitAnchor: lane — enforcement-pack's Lite-lane checks apply instead
rules.notes: Inapplicable rather than skipped, and the line says which check grades the lane instead so the reader is not left counting a missing verdict.

rules.summary: the branch is the trunk, where no feature declares Territory
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); docs/sdlc/repository-strategy.md; docs/sdlc/branch-strategy.md
rules.notes: CI runs on main too. This is the line that keeps a main build from reporting a scope pass it never made.

rules.summary: the branch is not NNN-shaped, so it maps to no spec directory
rules.law: CLAUDE.md Feature Structure; Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); docs/sdlc/repository-strategy.md
rules.emitAnchor: is not a numbered feature branch
rules.notes: The branch name is quoted back, because the name itself is the thing to fix.

rules.summary: a declared repository is not present in this checkout
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); docs/sdlc/repository-strategy.md; docs/sdlc/repository-strategy.md (nested layout)
rules.notes: The governance repository’s own CI looks exactly like this. Inert, and paired with the run-level line so the absence cannot read as a pass.

rules.summary: the declared directory is present but is not a git repository
rules.emitAnchor: n/a (present but not a git repository)
rules.notes: Reachable only through a '.git' file pointing at a gitdir that does not exist — an interrupted clone. A plain directory inside the governance tree takes the next rule instead, because git walks up.

rules.summary: the declared directory is part of the governance repository rather than a repository of its own
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); docs/sdlc/repository-strategy.md; docs/sdlc/repository-strategy.md
rules.emitAnchor: n/a (present but not a repository of its own
rules.notes: The dangerous one: git answers every question about it, just about the wrong history. Without the toplevel comparison the check would grade governance commits and report a confident verdict about code nobody wrote.

rules.summary: a declared repository has no branch of this feature’s name
rules.notes: The ordinary case of a feature that touches one of several repositories. Not a failure and not a pass — nothing here was graded, and the run says so.

rules.summary: under -All, no merge base with a trunk can be resolved
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); docs/sdlc/repository-strategy.md; feature 012 phase 1 review F5
rules.emitAnchor: UNGRADED could not resolve a merge base with a trunk
rules.notes: Code repositories are pre-existing and independent, so their trunk is often master or develop. NOTHING WAS GRADED is shouted because a silent skip here exempts a whole repository. WORD CHANGED in the phase-5 remediation (review F1): this site reported a run that graded nothing, and did it in a word that meant something else. The case is unchanged except for the verdict word it expects - the before-state is the previous revision of this rule's expected.txt, which is the D11 record for this conversion.

rules.summary: under -All, the range since the merge base is empty
rules.notes: An affirmative verdict that graded nothing. It is printed together with the run-level n/a on purpose: the PASS line alone is precisely the reading GAP-027 is about. WORD CHANGED in the phase-5 remediation (review F1): this site reported a run that graded nothing, and did it in a word that meant something else. The case is unchanged except for the verdict word it expects - the before-state is the previous revision of this rule's expected.txt, which is the D11 record for this conversion.

rules.summary: the commit named for grading does not resolve to a commit
rules.emitAnchor: ERROR '$Sha' does not resolve to a commit
rules.notes: Plain 'rev-parse --short' echoes an unknown sha back unvalidated, so the check asks for ^{commit}. A mistyped ref must not produce a verdict about nothing.

rules.summary: the commit is a merge commit, which authored nothing
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); docs/sdlc/repository-strategy.md; feature 012 D7
rules.notes: Grading a merge would charge one phase for every file both sides touched. Skipping it means this run graded nothing, which the run-level line then states.

rules.summary: the commit carries no 'phase N' token, so no declaration governs it
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); docs/sdlc/repository-strategy.md; docs/sdlc/branch-strategy.md (phase commits)
rules.notes: Territory is declared per phase. Without the token there is no declaration to compare against, and inventing one would be worse than saying so.

rules.summary: every path in the commit is inside the declared territory
rules.notes: The affirmative verdict, covered from the Micro side: ', Micro territory from spec.md' is the only thing in the output that says the declaration came from a mini-spec rather than from tasks.md. Mirrors REPOS-022 deliberately — one lane each.

rules.summary: a path in the commit is outside the declared territory
rules.notes: Gate 4 reaching the code. The remediation line beside it spells out the ordering that makes an amendment legitimate: a governance commit BEFORE the code phase commit.

rules.summary: a Micro feature declares no usable Territory block in its mini-spec
rules.law: constitution X (Micro lane); Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); docs/sdlc/repository-strategy.md
rules.emitAnchor: this Micro feature declares no usable **Territory** block
rules.notes: A hard FAIL where the Standard lane WARNs, and deliberately so: the mini-spec template requires the block, so no pre-Micro history exists to grandfather.

rules.summary: more than one Territory marker governs the phase
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); docs/sdlc/repository-strategy.md; feature 006 review F8
rules.emitAnchor: more than one **Territory** marker for phase $phaseN in $source
rules.notes: Two declarations are an ambiguous one, not a wider one. A grader that took the first would be choosing which rule to apply.

rules.summary: a territory entry is absolute or escapes the repository
rules.emitAnchor: invalid territory entry '$bad' (entries must be repo-relative
rules.notes: Matching is against repo-prefixed, repo-relative paths, so such an entry can never match anything — a declaration that silently declares nothing.

rules.summary: a Territory marker is declared with an empty entry list
rules.emitAnchor: but the entry list is empty (declare the paths, or remove the marker)
rules.notes: Distinct from declaring none at all, which is the compatibility WARN. Here the author said "this is my territory" and named nothing.

rules.summary: the Territory declaration post-dates the code commit it would legalise
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); docs/sdlc/repository-strategy.md; feature 012 FR-004, owner adjudication 2026-09-09
rules.notes: The cross-repository anti-retroactivity rule. Without it, 'commit the code, declare the territory afterwards' is a permanently green gate. Its message quotes the commit’s own instant, which is why the harness normalises <DATE>.

rules.summary: a '**Territory**' line carries no colon, so it declares nothing and says nothing
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); docs/sdlc/repository-strategy.md; feature 015 T019a; GAP-026
rules.emitAnchor: begins '**Territory**' but has no ':' on that line
rules.notes: What an author writes when the annotation wraps. Reported with its line number rather than falling through to the compatibility WARN, so the two graders agree about a malformed marker as well as a well-formed one.

rules.summary: this phase declares no Territory while another phase in the same file does
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); docs/sdlc/repository-strategy.md; feature 012 FR-015
rules.emitAnchor: but another phase in that file declares one
rules.notes: Not a document predating the convention — an omission in one phase of a document that knows it. Treating the two alike is how an undeclared phase commit reached exit 0 graded against nothing.

rules.summary: no Territory is declared anywhere in the document, at this date or since
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); docs/sdlc/repository-strategy.md; feature 012 FR-015
rules.emitAnchor: at this commit's date or since (non-blocking
rules.notes: The compatibility WARN, for a history predating the convention. The price of that mercy is a run that graded nothing, which the run-level line states outright.

rules.summary: a territory entry names a first segment that is neither a declared repository nor a governance path
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); docs/sdlc/repository-strategy.md; feature 012 C10
rules.notes: A probable typo. It would match no path and narrow the declaration in silence, so it is reported even when the run passes on the entry beside it.

rules.summary: the run graded nothing in any declared code repository
rules.law: Definition of Done gate 4 (scope); docs/sdlc/repository-strategy.md; feature 012 phase 1 review F6; GAP-027
rules.emitAnchor: UNGRADED (nothing was graded in the declared code repositories
rules.notes: The run-level verdict. Every inert line above it is a reason, and this is what stops a run made entirely of reasons from exiting 0 with no verdict in it. Suppressed as soon as one repository is actually graded. WORD CHANGED in the phase-5 remediation (review F1): this site reported a run that graded nothing, and did it in a word that meant something else. The case is unchanged except for the verdict word it expects - the before-state is the previous revision of this rule's expected.txt, which is the D11 record for this conversion.

rules.summary: a required kit path is missing from the tree
rules.law: CLAUDE.md Feature Structure; adoption/greenfield.md step 0; feature 007 research D2
rules.notes: The only one of doc-lint’s conditions computed inline rather than accumulated. A copy that skipped dot-directories leaves the agent without the /speckit.* commands, and an agent without them improvises a structure of its own.

rules.summary: a shipped file matches no manifest entry
rules.notes: update-kit.ps1 decides what to overwrite from this record, so an unclassified file is a file whose fate during an update nobody has decided.

rules.summary: two manifest entries of equal specificity claim one file with different classes
rules.notes: Neither entry is more specific, so there is no rule for choosing — and a silent choice means update-kit.ps1 overwriting a file the manifest also calls hand-merged.

rules.summary: the winning manifest entry names a class that is not one of the four
rules.law: feature 004 FR-002; adoption/updating.md (verbatim | surgical | generated | kit-only)
rules.notes: Found in feature 015 phase 1: a misspelt class counted as classified, so a typo bought silence instead of a verdict and no flow-down rule applied to the file.

rules.summary: kit-manifest.json is absent, so the completeness sweep cannot run
rules.notes: Fires alongside DOC-001, and both are true: the manifest is a required kit path AND the record this sweep reads.

rules.summary: a path referenced by a governance document does not resolve
rules.law: README (“Conventions this kit fixes at birth”); GAP-007 (the bold-reference convention)
rules.notes: doc-lint’s headline rule and the reason the script exists: a rule pointing at a file nobody can open has already drifted from reality. The report names file, line and reference — SC-008 in miniature.

rules.summary: unfilled {{SLOT}} / TODO(...) markers remain, and -FailOnSlots makes that fatal
rules.law: adoption/greenfield.md steps 1-3; feature 007 (the doctor FAILs unfilled slots after ratification)
rules.notes: One emission site, two verdicts, chosen by the caller: INFO while the kit template still ships its slots, ERROR once a project has ratified. Invisible to BOTH coverage passes before T030 — the precise pass looked for "ERROR and the recall sweep for a literal FAIL|ERROR, and this line spells its verdict with a variable.

rules.summary: the manifest completeness sweep declines in an adopted project, and says so
rules.law: adoption/updating.md §4; constitution X (the kit grades itself, an adopter grades its own work)
rules.notes: Two sites, one rule: the sweep declining and the sweep reporting are the two arms of one condition, and the directions cover one each. The declining arm is the phase 4 review's F1 — an INERT verdict that sat outside the declaration and outside the recall sweep at once, so it could never surface even as UNCLASSIFIED, and doc-lint reported a perfect 7 of 7 against a denominator built from the part already covered. That is the sentence this feature's own commit message wrote about T028; it was true one script over.

rules.summary: the affirmative run verdict — nothing missing, every referenced path resolves
rules.law: README (“Conventions this kit fixes at birth”)
rules.notes: An OK line is not a printer. It prints no accumulator; it asserts that the conditions above it did not occur, and on a green run it is the whole of what a reader sees. Its FAIL counterparts stay out of the denominator because those DO print a count the accumulator already holds — the asymmetry is deliberate and matches roadmap-claim-check.ps1.

rules.summary: a required kit path is missing from the adoption
rules.notes: Two sites, one rule: the FAIL and the ok are the two arms of one condition, and the directions cover one each. Same seventeen paths as doc-lint.ps1 with a different fix pointer — doc-lint speaks for the kit, the doctor for the adoption.

rules.summary: a project-owned (surgical) file still carries unfilled {{SLOT}} / TODO( markers
rules.notes: Two sites, one rule. Only manifest class surgical is scanned, and kit-shipped templates, the tier menu and modules/** are exempt — instructional markers there are the product, not an unfinished adoption (feature 007 review F1).

rules.summary: kit-manifest.json is absent, so project-owned files cannot be resolved
rules.notes: Reported by dimension 2 as well as dimension 1, and both are true: it is a required kit path AND the record that says which files the project owns.

rules.summary: the constitution still carries template markers
rules.law: constitution I; adoption/greenfield.md step 1/2; feature 007 contract specs/007-adoption-doctor/contracts/verify-kit-cli.md
rules.notes: Two sites, one rule. Matches the generic TODO( because speckit.constitution writes deferred fields as TODO(<FIELD>) (feature 007 review F5). A missing constitution is dimension 1’s finding, not this one’s.

rules.summary: kit-adoption.json is absent
rules.law: feature 007 contract specs/007-adoption-doctor/contracts/verify-kit-cli.md; feature 007 research D8 (grandfather posture)
rules.notes: WARN, not FAIL. Every adoption predating feature 007 has no record, and failing a project for being older than the check is not an audit, it is a trap.

rules.summary: kit-adoption.json does not parse as JSON
rules.notes: Unlike its absence this is a FAIL: a record that cannot be read is not history, it is breakage.

rules.summary: the record declares a schemaVersion this doctor does not understand
rules.emitAnchor: is not 1 (newer record than this doctor?)
rules.notes: Reading unknown fields with old rules is how a doctor reports green about a shape it never saw.

rules.summary: the record has no projectName
rules.notes: The field that makes a record about a project rather than a file that happens to parse.

rules.summary: the record topology is neither single nor multi
rules.notes: Topology decides whether missing codeRepos matters, so an unrecognised value leaves the doctor unable to judge the next finding.

rules.summary: the record declares no tiers
rules.notes: Tiers bind a project to its rulebooks. A project with none has no craft layer the doctor can check.

rules.summary: a declared tier name cannot address a rulebook file
rules.emitAnchor: is not a valid tier name
rules.notes: Custom tiers are first-class (docs/rulebooks/README.md; feature 007 phase 4 review F3), so the doctor polices the NAME, never the meaning.

rules.summary: a declared tier has no instantiated rulebook
rules.notes: A project claiming a craft layer it does not have. The fix pointer differs for a known tier and a custom one; the fixture pins the known arm.

rules.summary: codeRepos is present but is not an array
rules.notes: The same field, the same rule, in two scripts — here and in scope-check-repos.ps1 — because a code repository’s own CI may run one and never the other.

rules.summary: a codeRepos entry is not a plain directory name
rules.emitAnchor: is not a plain directory name
rules.notes: A path, a traversal or a drive prefix addresses a tree outside the governance root.

rules.summary: a declared code repository is not present in this checkout
rules.notes: WARN: a governance-only checkout is a legitimate reason to see this, and it is the same state scope-check-repos.ps1 reports as n/a rather than as a failure.

rules.summary: a multi-repo adoption declares no code repositories
rules.notes: Nothing is broken and nothing is checked either: gate 4 never reaches the code and the phase commits are reviewer-verified only. This WARN is what breaks that silence.

rules.summary: the developers declaration is present and unusable
rules.notes: The check falls back to solo silently by design; the doctor is the half that tells the project its declaration is being ignored. Both read scripts/adoption-lib.ps1 — the two copies drifted once already, and a comment asserting they matched is what let it through.

rules.summary: the developers declaration is usable, and the doctor states which evidence arm is in force
rules.notes: Absence is NOT a finding — an adoption predating feature 013 declares nothing and is treated as solo, the stricter arm — so the fail direction is the field’s absence and the line simply does not appear.

rules.summary: no gate proof with exit code 0 is recorded
rules.emitAnchor: no gate proof with exit code 0
rules.notes: A gate that has never been green is not a gate. The record must carry evidence the ritual ran, not a promise that it would.

rules.summary: the adoption record is valid in every respect dimension 4 checks
rules.notes: Composed from everything the dimension checked — tiers joined, code repositories named, gate proven — and withdrawn entirely if any one condition fails, because a half-valid record is not a valid record.

rules.summary: .kit-version holds update-kit’s JSON record
rules.notes: The healthy shape, and the one the pin is actually written in.

rules.summary: .kit-version holds a bare commit token
rules.notes: adoption/updating.md tells a human to create one this way, so it is accepted — and distinguished in the message rather than collapsed into the JSON case, because only one of the two carries a version.

rules.summary: .kit-version is neither shape — hand-edited or empty
rules.notes: The first version of this rule was validated against a bare-sha fixture update-kit never writes, so it was right about a file that did not exist. The three fixtures here pin both real shapes and the refusal.

rules.summary: .kit-version is absent
rules.notes: WARN: a project adopted by copy and never updated is behind, not broken.

rules.summary: -Root names a directory that does not exist
rules.notes: Fail-fast before five dimensions of confident findings about a tree nobody has. The only rule in the suite whose case needs the harness to point -Root somewhere other than the fixture (command.json rootSuffix).

rules.summary: the tree is the kit template itself, not an adoption
rules.law: feature 007 contract specs/007-adoption-doctor/contracts/verify-kit-cli.md; feature 007 research D5.1 / D5.3, review F2
rules.emitAnchor: not applicable (this is the kit template
rules.notes: A kit full of unfilled slots is the product. An adoption record VETOES the decline, and the pass direction is that veto: without it a project could exempt itself from its own doctor by copying one heading.

rules.summary: the affirmative run verdict — adoption integrity verified across all five dimensions
rules.notes: The line an adopted project's CI prints on every green run, and the one most readers of the doctor ever see. Same reasoning as DOC-009, and the same asymmetry: the FAIL summary beside it prints $failCount and $warnCount and stays a printer.

rules.summary: there is no origin remote, so there is no claim ledger
rules.emitAnchor: 'roadmap-claims: n/a (no origin remote — no claim ledger to check against)'
rules.notes: Declining OUT LOUD is the requirement: a silent exit 0 here is indistinguishable from a roadmap that is actually honest.

rules.summary: origin is configured and cannot be reached
rules.emitAnchor: 'roadmap-claims: n/a (origin unreachable — cannot read the claim ledger)'
rules.notes: Kept distinct from having no remote at all: one is a state of the project, the other a state of the machine, and the reader needs different things from each.

rules.summary: the ledger holds no numbered claims
rules.notes: An OK rather than an n/a: the ledger WAS read and it is empty, which is a verdict rather than a declined one.

rules.summary: the tree has no docs/roadmap.md
rules.notes: An adopter roadmap is adopter-authored and may not exist. The check declines rather than manufacturing a failure out of a file the project never promised — the verify-kit precedent.

rules.summary: no roadmap table carries a Status column
rules.emitAnchor: 'roadmap-claims: n/a (docs/roadmap.md has no table with a Status column)'
rules.notes: The kit knows the shape of its own roadmap and will not read a status out of a table that has none. Naming the missing column is what lets an adopter choose to adopt the shape.

rules.summary: a claim on origin is mentioned by no roadmap row
rules.notes: GAP-017 itself: in the first post-010 field use a feature sat thirteen days with an approved spec and a gated phase while main said nothing about it. The remedy in the message is the ritual — flip the row in a MAIN-SIDE commit at claim time, never only on the branch.

rules.summary: a claim is on the roadmap and its row still reads idea
rules.notes: The subtler half, and the likelier to be trusted: the feature IS on the roadmap, so a human skimming it believes the status. Worse than an absence, which at least looks like a gap.

rules.summary: every claim but the branch’s own is visible with a non-idea row
rules.notes: The affirmative verdict, and it names the exempted number. A branch is exempt for its OWN claim so a fresh claim’s first CI run cannot deadlock on a row the same change is about to flip — stating the exemption is what stops it being mistaken for coverage.

rules.summary: there is no origin remote to compare claims against
rules.law: docs/sdlc/team-workflow.md rule 5 (overlap is sequenced, not forbidden); feature 003 contract specs/003-flow-efficiency-pack/contracts/territory-check-cli.md
rules.notes: Declines rather than printing CLEAN, which would be a claim that nothing overlaps made by a run that looked at nothing.

rules.summary: the branch shares no file with any open feature branch
rules.law: docs/sdlc/team-workflow.md rule 5 (overlap is sequenced, not forbidden); feature 003 contract specs/003-flow-efficiency-pack/contracts/territory-check-cli.md
rules.notes: The affirmative verdict names the branch it is about. On a team a bare CLEAN would not say whose territory was checked, which is the only part that matters.

rules.summary: the branch shares files with another open feature branch
rules.law: docs/sdlc/team-workflow.md rule 5 (overlap is sequenced, not forbidden); feature 003 contract specs/003-flow-efficiency-pack/contracts/territory-check-cli.md
rules.notes: Names the other branch, its staleness and every shared path: an overlap whose files you cannot see is an overlap nobody can sequence.

rules.summary: at least one overlapping claim is live
rules.law: docs/sdlc/team-workflow.md rule 5 (overlap is sequenced, not forbidden); feature 003 contract specs/003-flow-efficiency-pack/contracts/territory-check-cli.md
rules.notes: The kit’s whole stance on shared territory, and the reason exit 2 is advisory. A check that simply refused would push two owners into working around it.

rules.summary: every overlapping claim is stale and therefore reclaimable
rules.law: docs/sdlc/team-workflow.md rule 5 (overlap is sequenced, not forbidden); feature 003 contract specs/003-flow-efficiency-pack/contracts/territory-check-cli.md; team-workflow rule 3
rules.notes: Exit 0, not 2: a claim nobody is working can be adopted, and blocking on it would make an abandoned branch a permanent obstacle. The pair differs only in the age of one commit.

rules.summary: the JSON contract answers when there is no remote
rules.law: docs/sdlc/team-workflow.md rule 5 (overlap is sequenced, not forbidden); feature 003 contract specs/003-flow-efficiency-pack/contracts/territory-check-cli.md
rules.notes: The one place this script’s machine output says less than its prose: a JSON caller cannot tell “nothing overlaps” from “nothing was checked”. Pinned as it stands and recorded as a finding — the contract belongs to feature 003, not to this phase.

rules.summary: the JSON report carries the branch, the verdict and every overlap
rules.law: docs/sdlc/team-workflow.md rule 5 (overlap is sequenced, not forbidden); feature 003 contract specs/003-flow-efficiency-pack/contracts/territory-check-cli.md
rules.notes: Built by a different code path from the prose report and carrying the same facts, which is the property worth pinning. The anchor names the ConvertTo-Json line rather than the object literal above it: the emission spans two source lines and the scanner reads one line at a time, which the anchor-ambiguity assertion reported as 0 sites rather than letting the entry measure nothing.

rules.summary: each member announces itself by name before it runs
rules.notes: The member names are this wrapper’s entire interface: branch protection names one required check, adopted-project docs quote these names, and SC-005 is the promise that they do not move. The pair differs by whether the tree is adopted, because that is the only thing that changes which members exist.

rules.summary: each member gets exactly one verdict line
rules.notes: Never short-circuits: a failing member does not stop the others, because one run must report every problem rather than the first. Three verdicts share this one site — OK, FAIL, and the member’s own n/a reason lifted out of its output.

rules.summary: the adoption doctor did not run, and the run says so rather than omitting it
rules.notes: The gate mirrors the doctor’s own discriminator (.kit-version OR kit-adoption.json). A silent omission would leave a reader counting six verdicts where the documentation promises seven, unable to tell a skipped check from a forgotten one — SC-004 at the wrapper level.

rules.summary: at least one member failed, and the run fails with it
rules.notes: The count is failing members out of members that RAN, which is what separates “one thing broke” from “the tree did”. The fail fixture puts two inert members beside the failing one: an n/a must neither mask a failure nor be counted as a pass, and the line reads 1 of 6 rather than 1 of 4.

rules.summary: every member that ran exited 0
rules.notes: The one line a CI badge reads. Printed once, last, and after every member’s own verdict — never instead of them. Its pass fixture is a run whose members include two inert ones, because “nothing failed” and “everything was checked” are different claims and only the first is being made.

rules.summary: the machine half of gate 5 has no diff base, so it inspects no review file and says so
rules.law: DoD gate 5; constitution I; roadmap GAP-027
rules.notes: GAP-027's canonical site. This was a bare `return`: the check stopped before listing a single candidate and the run printed OK. Both directions carry the SAME review file - no provenance section, no attestation, the implementer named as reviewer - and differ only in whether the base resolves. The pass direction therefore shows the exact violation the fail direction let through, which is a stronger statement than an absence. UNGRADED, never FAIL: FR-011 forbids a new hard failure on this lane (plan D6).

rules.summary: the Lite lane's guards grade an EMPTY file list because no base resolves
rules.notes: The one member that does not DECLINE on a null base - it grades, and grades nothing, which passes the way an empty accusation is never proved. The pack's own comment said it before this phase did: a baseless 'fix/' branch touching anything at all went green. The fixture touches a dependency manifest, a prohibited category, and the pass direction reports it. A vacuous grade reaches the same wrong verdict as a skipped one and is named the same way.

rules.summary: the Micro phase walk has no diff base, so 'exactly one phase' and the line bound compare nothing
rules.notes: Reached through the unreadable-parent state ('truncateCommit'), which is why that fixture capability exists: a corrupt BLOB is met by a check that reads a file out of history, and a check that walks the commit graph never touches one. The fail direction also shows the combined verdict - AmendmentAuthority FAILS for want of a base while three other members report UNGRADED - which is the shape the runner prints ungraded lines independently of the verdict word to support.

rules.summary: no commit is measured against the phase-size guideline because no base resolves
rules.notes: The advisory member, included deliberately. A check whose only output is a WARN still has an opinion to fail to form, and leaving it out would have said that an advisory check is not worth knowing the status of - the same reasoning that pulled PhaseSizeWarning itself into the denominator in phase 3. Depth-1 clone, the ordinary actions/checkout shape.

rules.summary: a member ran and formed no opinion, and the run says so instead of OK
rules.notes: The aggregator half of GAP-027. enforcement-pack can now report UNGRADED; this is the rule that the single entry point an adopted project runs does not print RESULT OK over the top of it. Exit 0 in BOTH directions, asserted by both cases: the verdict changes and the exit code does not, which is the whole of plan D6. Built on stub members, like every other RIT case, so it tests the aggregation and not the member.

rules.summary: every commit on the branch was skipped, so the run graded nothing and says so
rules.notes: The general case the per-site conversions do not reach. Invoke-ScopeCheck returns a skip for a merge commit, for a commit with no 'phase N' token, and for a pre-006 tree with no tasks.md; a branch made only of those exits 0 having graded nothing, and before this the wrapper printed OK. Counted the way scripts/scope-check-repos.ps1 has counted since feature 012 ($graded), so the two members answer the same question the same way. The pair differs in one commit's SUBJECT LINE - 'work: the thing' against 'phase 1: the thing' - which is the whole of the condition (plan D10).

rules.summary: the ungraded state is lifted for every member that can reach it, not only the first
rules.notes: Added in the phase-5 remediation (review F1). $ungradedCapableMembers is an allow-list, so the mechanism RIT-006 proves is silently inert for any member left out of it - which is how scope-check shipped its own GAP-027 fail-open through a phase that existed to close GAP-027. This case stubs scope-check instead of enforcement-pack and asserts the same three things: the word on the member's line, the word on the RESULT line, exit 0. It fails if a future edit drops a name from that list, which RIT-006 would not notice. The anchor is the same emission site RIT-006 names, and that is deliberate rather than sloppy: the allow-list is not itself an emission site, and the site it governs is this one. RIT-006 asks whether the line can be printed at all; RIT-007 asks whether it is printed for the second member to reach the state. One site, two rules, said out loud - the inventory allows it and the ambiguity check counts hits per rule, not rules per hit.

rules.summary: a range with no commits in it is reported as graded-nothing, not returned from in silence
rules.notes: Found by the phase 6 coverage sweep, not by reading: the site has existed since feature 014 and no fixture reached it. It is GAP-027's shape inside the check that grades amendments - a return that grades nothing. The pair reaches it through -ReplayBase/-ReplayTip (014 plan D2c), the supported way to hand the check an explicit range; HEAD..HEAD is the empty one and HEAD~1..HEAD the nearest non-empty one, which is the whole of the difference (plan D10).

rules.summary: the trunk is not a lane, and the dispatch says so rather than printing a bare OK
rules.emitAnchor: is the trunk, not a feature/fix/chore/docs branch
rules.notes: Nothing in the suite asserted this line before phase 6: 49 expectations end on enforcement-pack OK and not one of them was a trunk run, so a dispatch that stopped printing the reason would have been invisible. The pair differs in the branch named (plan D10).

rules.summary: a commit rev-list yields but the metadata batch did not parse fails the check rather than being skipped
rules.emitAnchor: AmendmentAuthority: could not parse commit metadata for
rules.exemption: Requires git rev-list to list a commit that Get-CommitMetaBatch then fails to parse - the two reading the same object store and disagreeing. The fixture model can corrupt an object (truncateCommit), but a corrupt commit makes rev-list fail first, so the run never reaches this branch. Reaching it needs a partially readable object, which the recipe cannot build and which would not be stable across git versions if it could. Exempted rather than faked: a fixture that reached a different failure and called it this one would be the inventory lying.
rules.notes: Exempted in phase 6 (T045, FR-004). The site stays inventoried so it cannot be reworded away unnoticed.

rules.summary: a commit whose committer date cannot be read fails the repository rather than being graded
rules.emitAnchor: ERROR cannot read the committer date of
rules.exemption: Needs git show -s --format=%cI <sha> to return empty for a commit that rev-list already yielded and the earlier guards accepted. Every way the fixture model can break a commit object breaks it earlier in the same run, so the case would pin a different rule under this rule's name. Same reasoning as AMEND-007.
rules.notes: Exempted in phase 6 (T045, FR-004).

rules.summary: an unexpected exception inside the doctor is reported as ERROR and exits 1 rather than escaping
rules.exemption: A defensive catch around the whole doctor. Its message is whatever exception reached it, so an expectation could only pin the text of some OTHER defect - and a fixture that deliberately caused one would be asserting that defect, not this handler. What the handler guarantees (no unhandled escape, exit 1) is a property of every other verify-kit case, all 27 of which would fail loudly if it broke.
rules.notes: Exempted in phase 6 (T045, FR-004).

rules.summary: a run started outside a git repository is refused rather than answered
rules.exemption: territory-check.ps1 reports its error paths with Write-Error (or Write-Warning) under its own ErrorActionPreference = Stop, which makes the write TERMINATING: the script dies there and the exit 1 written after each one is unreachable. Measured through the harness, the run produces the launcher's own line and exit 97 (did not run to a verdict), not the script's message and not exit 1. A fixture could pin that, but it would be asserting RunChild.ps1's behaviour rather than the rule's, and 97 is documented as a code no kit script emits. Recorded as a finding instead - specs/015-enforcement-assurance/notes.md, phase 6, awaiting promotion to a roadmap GAP row (docs/roadmap.md is outside this phase's Territory) - and NOT worked around here, because scripts/territory-check.ps1 is outside phase 6's Territory and this phase may not change it.
rules.notes: Exempted in phase 6 (T045, FR-004). Five sites, one cause; the fix is a roadmap item this phase records and may not itself write.
